correctness.rationale: The standard zonotope center is half the degree vector and is the unique circumcenter by central symmetry. At an acyclic-orientation vertex, the centered coordinate is one half of indegree minus outdegree. Expanding its squared norm gives a fixed degree-square term minus the total number of directed two-edge paths. For a complete multipartite graph, every triple in three distinct parts contributes unavoidably once, while a two-in-one-part triple contributes exactly when the singleton interleaves the equal-part pair in a topological order. Thus the norm is maximized exactly by block orders of the parts. The remaining symmetric-polynomial simplification gives the displayed cubic-moment formula, and central symmetry gives the diameter.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphical zonotopes form a natural iterated-shuffle family in the recent deformed-permutahedron literature and interpolate between complete-bipartite zonotopes and the permutahedron. The theorem gives their exact outer Euclidean size for arbitrary part sizes, classifies every sphere-contact vertex, and translates the metric extremum into a clean noninterleaving condition on acyclic orientations. The cubic-moment formula and exact \(k!\) equality class are structural family-wide facts, not a finite census or a routine specialization of an existing metric theorem.
